senses.gloss: (b. h.) to be pliable, soft, tender.—[B. Kam. 80ᵃ הענוגה Ar. s. v. ענג 2, mistaken reading for העגונה, v. עָגַן.]—Denom. עוֹנֶג.

units: <cite ref="Tosefta Ma'aser Sheni 2:1">Tosef. Maas. Sh. II, 1</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Terumot 10:4">Tosef. Ter. X, 4</cite> <he>מְענֶּגֶת שערה וכ׳</he> (Var. <he>מעגנת</he>, <he>מעגלת</he>, v. <cite ref="P00105"><he>עָגַן</he></cite>, <cite ref="P00089"><he>עָגַל</he></cite>) she may soften her hair by pressing it against her (the priest’s daughter’s) hair.

senses.gloss: (denom. of עוֹנֶג, with ref. to Is. LVIII, 13, ‘and callest the Sabbath a delight’) to celebrate pleasurably, to enjoy.
units: <cite ref="Shabbat 118b:2">Sabb. 118ᵇ</cite> <he>כל המְעַנֵּג את השבת וכ׳</he> to him who observes the Sabbath with enjoyments, his heart’s desires are granted.
<cite ref="Shabbat 118b:2">Ib.</cite> <he>במה מְעַנְּגוֹ</he> wherewith does one make it enjoyable? Tanḥ.
<cite ref="Pesikta Rabbati 23">Pesik. R. s. 23</cite>, end <he>ובשבת הם באים ומְעַנְּגִים</he> (prob. to be read: <he>ומִתְעַנְּגִים</he>) and on the Sabbath they come and enjoy themselves.

senses.gloss: to enjoy one’s self; to indulge in luxuries. Ib. כל שהוא מִתְעַנֵּג בשבת שואל וכ׳ whoever enjoys the Sabbath may ask, and the Lord will grant (v. supra).
units: <cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 149:1-3">Midr. Till. to Ps. CXLIX</cite> <he>בא … הצדיקים מִתְעַנְּגִים</he> come and see how the righteous enjoy luxuries (in the hereafter).

<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 149:3">Ib.</cite> <he>והם מתענגים ואומרים וכ׳</he> and they act like persons used to comforts, saying, it is impossible to sleep in this bed &c.; a. e.—[<cite ref="Devarim Rabbah 7">Deut. R. s. 7</cite>, end <he>היו מתענגים וכ׳</he> they enjoyed themselves by rolling in the flavored grass; prob. to be read: <he>מִתְעַגְּגִים</he> fr. <cite ref="P00079"><he>עגג</he></cite>, v. <cite ref="C01182"><he>גִּעְגֵּעַ</he></cite>.]
